bluf: Page One Power is a founder led link building and SEO agency in Boise, founded in 2010 by Jon Ball, the CEO, and Zach Ball, that sells hand built links from an all US team and, by its own claim, never uses AI generated content. Its newest lines point to AI search: a GEO page with a five step process and a LinkedIn company ad selling AI Search Optimization. It lists no dated moves, news or open jobs. A rival should know its AI search line has no client proof in the record: the newest case study is dated 2024-12-10.
doing:
The positioning line, a Boise link building agency earning real links through custom content and human outreach, plus SEO, digital PR, technical SEO and AI search optimization, decodes as a link building shop that writes content other sites will cite and pitches it by hand, with search services sold around that core. The headline claim, building links since 2010 with an all US team using human outreach instead of automated link blasts, is a quality promise resting on tenure, onshore staff and manual work, quoted as a claim.

The sold mix is narrow, breadth 3, with every family outside Search & AI visibility at 0. It leads with Content & Digital PR at 3, where the H1 brands it the link builders and the record lists custom, enterprise and white label link building, linkable assets and digital PR, and with SEO at 3, where the title and meta frame it as an SEO company selling SEO, technical SEO, keyword research and consulting. AI Search / GEO scores 2 on a dedicated page with a five step process, promoted by a LinkedIn ad. The one proprietary name, SEO Blueprint, carries no description, and the record lists no partners.

The AI posture treats AI search as a destination, built on earned links and structured content, while stressing that it never uses AI generated content; AI Automation / Agents scores 0. The record lists no dated moves, no news and 0 jobs on its BambooHR board, and the newest dated case study is YorkTest on 2024-12-10. Pricing sits in a downloadable 2025 pricing sheet with no prices captured. Conspicuously absent for a technical SEO seller: any feed, schema or entity work despite the structured content claim, any measurement line, and any case study describing AI search results.
clients:
The ICP reads as mixed, and the record lists four verticals: B2B SaaS and IT software, personal finance, consumer health testing and portable storage. The home market is the US, served from Boise.

The needs read holds 7 named clients, 6 observed and 1 names only, all from case study evidence, with organic demand at 0.857 of the mix. YorkTest came for a page one ranking on a target query (YorkTest Case Study, 2024-12-10). Domotz came for traffic, and its case study credits an 18% YoY rise in domain traffic (2023-09-28). Kreo, a SaaS platform, ran a 6 month SEO campaign on keyword rich content and link building, with gains in organic traffic, rankings and domain clicks stated without figures (2023-10-11); its B2B pipeline code reflects the client type, not pipeline work. Fiscal Tiger bought content creation and link building, credited with growing organic traffic from nothing to 65,000 monthly visitors, and Bedly bought content consultation and link building, credited with a 9,000% rise in top 100 keyword rankings within 6 months, both dated 2020-04-02; the web build code on Fiscal Tiger has no build work behind it in the excerpt. Atera carries only an seo URL slug. BigSteelBox is the names only client, though its 2023-07-19 excerpt describes rising in the SERPs for moving and storage queries, which reads as organic demand.

No client sits on another tracked agency's book. What the base needs next: these clients bought rankings and traffic, and under KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) they will likely need presence in AI answers, which no case study in the record shows it delivering (moderate confidence).
house: Say and do: one line tested, and it holds. The AI Search / GEO test is corroborated: it publishes llms.txt and its sitemap holds 16 AI topic URLs, so the verdict counts 1 of 1 tested lines practised, and the Radar lists no gaps. Publishing cadence was not measured; the sitemap lists 665 URLs with 0 updated in 90 days and 0 in 365, and the record holds no recent blog dates. No AI crawlers are blocked. The stack is HubSpot CMS with gtm, ga4, a Meta pixel, HubSpot tracking and Microsoft Clarity, and no test tools or ABM stack. Its Transparency Center record shows 14 Google ads, 1 in the last 30 days (4 text, 6 image, 4 video), last shown 2026-09-01, under the advertiser name Zach Ball. LinkedIn shows 2 company page ads, one titled AI Search Optimization Service, the other pitching custom link building to sites struggling with rankings.
market:
The Horus read scores Page One Power 11.1 on the tailwind index, Favored band but percentile 47. It is best placed for KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation (net 0.438, driven by AI Search / GEO), and KJ8, human provenance becomes a distribution signal (net 0.253), which its no AI content stance fits. Its largest exposure outweighs both: KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out (net -0.506, SEO and Content & Digital PR), then KJ9 (net -0.328). It best fits The Toll Road at 88/100, and is partial on P1, unknown on P5, and absent on P2, P6 and P7.

The Monsoon read is 70.7, band Landfall, percentile 92, with displacement 74.7 above migration 66.7. The verdict puts 67 of it in the sold mix, SEO (34) and Content & Digital PR (21) carrying the most movable hours, and sends the work 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. The evidence class is observed, driven by its white label line; no offshore hub is listed, and its own words claim onshore delivery.
openings:
The strongest opening is proof. Page One Power sells AI Search Optimization and practises it on its own site, but none of the 9 case studies in its record describes AI search work, and the newest is dated 2024-12-10. A rival with dated citation results is likely, moderate confidence, to win SaaS and IT software buyers weighing AI visibility offers, since P1 is only partial. Falsifier: a dated AI search case study naming a client on pageonepower.com.

Price is the second front. Displacement at 74.7 on the Monsoon read and an observed white label line mean agencies reselling its links likely buy on price, so an offshore delivered rival can undercut it there; with direct buyers, its all US, human outreach claim and the KJ8 tailwind make undercutting only a roughly even chance.

KJ6 is its largest exposure, and breadth 3 leaves adjacent ground open: schema and entity work (P2 absent) and measurement (Data & Measurement at 0). No client is shared with another tracked agency, so every account is a cold approach. Before pricing against it, a rival should obtain the 2025 pricing sheet.
